component: Folder UI and database lifetime boundary

quotes.text:
* In general, there is little potential downside to nulling out the message
   *  database reference when it is in use.  As long as someone is holding onto
   *  a message header from the database, the database will be kept open, and
   *  therefore the database service will still have a reference to the db.
   *  When the folder goes to ask for the database again, the service will have
   *  it, and it will not need to be re-opened.
   *
   * Note: regrettably a unit test cannot verify that we did this; msgDatabase
   *  is a getter that will always try and load the message database!

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The openFolder removal retires nsIMsgWindow.openFolder and the mail-session IsFolderOpenInWindow checks. Current databaseOpen is simply whether mDatabase is non-null. That state can be used by cache, search and autosync code without proving that a folder is visible. Preserve the distinction in names and comments; the retained database itself may also outlive the folder reference through message headers. This is static source evidence. No runtime, build, lint or live accessibility check was run. Full Bugzilla and Phabricator discussion remains pending.
title: Treat databaseOpen as a retained database reference rather than an open UI window
